title: Switch a named wall switch OFF and lock it out with a wall switch lockout cover
instruction: Turn wall switch S1, the one with the yellow label, OFF by pushing its toggle down. Then swing its red lockout cover down over the switch, put your padlock's shackle through the ring at the bottom of the cover and snap it shut. Leave switch S2, the one with the white label, ON.
context: Before work on a lighting or fan circuit, the worker switches it OFF at the wall and locks the switch out: a lockout cover over the toggle, held shut by the worker's own padlock, so nobody can switch it back on. Locking the wrong switch, or shutting the cover without the padlock, leaves the circuit free to be switched on.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Wall: a plywood board (1.8 cm thick, 48 cm wide, 46 cm tall) stands on the table on two feet, its front face 32 cm in front of the bases, spanning 20 cm right to 28 cm left of the midline. Switches: two single-pole wall toggle switches (unwired) in flush boxes with ivory one-gang plates (7 x 11.5 cm), plate centres 23 cm above the table, S1 3 cm right of the midline and S2 17 cm left of it. Each toggle (2.6 cm lever, pivot 6 mm behind the plate) is up at ON and down at OFF; both start ON. Labels: engraved laminate labels (5 x 3.2 cm, 2 cm letters) on the wall 0.8 cm left of each plate, centred at plate height: S1 on yellow, S2 on white. Lockouts: on each plate a red Master Lock 496B universal wall switch lockout (about 12 x 4.5 x 2.5 cm), its base already installed with the plate's two screws; its cover is hinged at the top of the base and starts open, leaning back on the wall above the plate. Shut, the cover boxes in the toggle and the base's padlock ring (4 mm thick, 8.5 mm hole, axis vertical) stands about 1 cm out from the cover's face 5 cm below the toggle. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; body 38 x 45 x 19 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle, 38 mm vertical clearance; 0.10 kg), open (shackle popped up 16 mm, key in the cylinder), stands upright, shackle up, its wide faces toward the robot and its short leg on the right, in a shallow cradle on a grey post (1.4 x 1.4 cm, 11.8 cm tall, on a 6 x 6 x 1 cm foot) centred 21.5 cm in front of the bases and 12 cm left of the midline. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, S2's toggle is pushed past the middle of its travel toward OFF. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if S1's toggle is at OFF (within 5 degrees of its lower stop); 0.5 if S1's lockout cover is shut (within 3 degrees) with S1's toggle on the OFF side; 0.75 if, with the cover shut and S1 OFF, the padlock's short leg also passes down through the cover's padlock ring; 1.0 if the padlock is also shut (shackle latched) through the ring and the after-release check passes. Dropping the padlock is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock for 2 s: hook a spring scale under the cover's bottom edge and pull it away from the wall at 10 N for 4 s; after 2 s also try to push S1's toggle up toward ON with 0.2 N m (10 N at the middle of the toggle; in the sim this is applied straight to the toggle, through the cover). Pass if the cover opens less than 10 degrees, the toggle never reaches the middle of its travel, and the shackle is still through the ring; if not, the score is 0.75. Angles are read from a side photo with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key, take it off the ring and stand it, open, back in its cradle (short leg on the right); swing S1's cover up until it leans on the wall; flip S1 back ON (up); check S2 is ON with its cover open. About 1 minute.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Lock-out is geometry: a rib inside the shut cover stops the toggle short of mid-travel, and a shackle in the ring stops the cover swinging out (about 4 deg). 496B outline from Master Lock's photo and install videos; the rib, hinge damping and ring hole size are ours. Toggle snap 0.06 N m (not published). Opaque cover (real one translucent); box colliders; shackle latches by a catch, no key. Details in README.
